title: Oracle Targets $225B in Annual Revenue by FY2030 and Caps New Capital Raises at $20B
summary:
The enterprise software firm projects that its non-GAAP earnings per share will reach at least $21 by fiscal 2030 as part of a strategy to scale its cloud infrastructure. Oracle is targeting annual revenue of more than $225 billion by that period, which would require a compound annual growth rate of over 35% and non-GAAP operating margins above 40%. To finance this expansion, the company will restrict new capital raises to $20 billion through FY30, split evenly between debt and equity, separate from a $20 billion equity raise completed in the first quarter of FY2027.

Oracle reaffirmed its FY2027 outlook, forecasting revenue of at least $90 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $8.10. The company anticipates that spending on AI data centers will peak in fiscal 2027 and 2028 before its growth becomes self-funded in FY2029. This projection includes a target to return to positive free cash flow in the second half of FY2028 and generate more than $30 billion by FY2029. Shares of Oracle rose more than 9% following the announcements.

• $10B in equity
